reason: A better supports the requested visitor-desk decision within the 180–260-word brief. Its opening paragraph rejects the withdrawn March target, its second distinguishes April's conditional proposal from passenger authorization, and its final paragraph provides booking prerequisites with source IDs. B reaches the same central decision but substantially exceeds the requested length, repeats information, and incorrectly dates the no-ticket statement to 1 February rather than 10 February.

task_fidelity.reason: Provides a suitably concise, dated English status note covering advertising, superseded plans, conditional proposals and booking checks, with source IDs.
task_fidelity.excerpt: Opening paragraph: “The new ferry **cannot** be advertised as available from 1 March.”
task_fidelity.source_evidence: S1: “the operator withdrew the 1 March target and proposed 15 April as the earliest possible passenger launch”.

facts_and_evidence.reason: Accurately attributes the dated operator changes and port status without inventing a confirmed launch.
facts_and_evidence.excerpt: Second paragraph: “No final passenger-service permission, confirmed timetable or booking release exists, and the vessel had not been delivered by 14 February (S2).”
facts_and_evidence.source_evidence: S2: “The vessel had not been delivered by the update. There is no final passenger-service permission, confirmed timetable or booking release.”

explanation_and_synthesis.reason: Connects the operator's withdrawal and outstanding conditions with the limited port permission to explain why neither date establishes availability.
explanation_and_synthesis.excerpt: Second paragraph: “The 15 April proposal is likewise not a current commitment: it is an earliest-possible date, conditional on outstanding items (S1).”
explanation_and_synthesis.source_evidence: S1 makes 15 April subject to “delivery, trials and final operating permission”; S2 permits only non-passenger trials.

counterevidence_and_boundaries.reason: Directly addresses the potentially misleading April proposal and March trial permission, preserving the distinction between proposals and authorized passenger service.
counterevidence_and_boundaries.excerpt: Second paragraph: “The port log allows only non-passenger trial sailings during March and expressly does not authorize carrying paying passengers (S2).”
counterevidence_and_boundaries.source_evidence: S2: “it does not authorize carrying paying passengers”; S1 describes April as the “earliest possible” launch.

reader_usefulness.reason: Gives an immediate advertising decision and a concrete, compact set of checks before bookings.
reader_usefulness.excerpt: Final paragraph: “Before accepting bookings, the desk must verify: vessel delivery; completion of trials; final passenger-service operating permission; a confirmed timetable; and formal booking release (S1, S2).”
reader_usefulness.source_evidence: S1 identifies delivery, trials and final operating permission as conditions; S2 records absent passenger permission, confirmed timetable and booking release.

task_fidelity.reason: Addresses the substantive questions and cites source IDs in references, but substantially exceeds the explicit 180–260-word requirement and needs significant condensation.
task_fidelity.excerpt: “Recommended handling”: “Do not market either date as a confirmed passenger service.” This follows separate decision, current-position, status-table and verification sections.
task_fidelity.source_evidence: S1 and S2 support the decision; the brief explicitly requests a “180–260-word English status note,” rather than the much longer submission.

facts_and_evidence.reason: The central chronology and authorization status are accurate, but the ticket-release statement is assigned to the wrong notice. Some wording also strengthens absence of confirmation into absence of publication.
facts_and_evidence.excerpt: “What must be verified before accepting bookings”: “no tickets had been released as of the 1 February notice”; “Confirmed timetable — not published.”
facts_and_evidence.source_evidence: S1 attaches “No tickets had been released as of that notice” to the 10 February notice, not 1 February. S2 states there is no “confirmed timetable,” not explicitly that none has been published.

explanation_and_synthesis.reason: Clearly explains the relationship between withdrawn plans, conditional targets and trial authorization, but repeats the synthesis across prose, a table, checks and recommendations.
explanation_and_synthesis.excerpt: Opening decision section: “Advertising a 1 March start would therefore market a superseded plan as a current commitment.”
explanation_and_synthesis.source_evidence: S1 explicitly withdraws the March target on 10 February and substitutes a conditional earliest April target; S2 supplies no passenger authorization.

counterevidence_and_boundaries.reason: Explicitly rejects interpreting either the April proposal or March trials as confirmed passenger availability and preserves the log's lack of a completion forecast.
counterevidence_and_boundaries.excerpt: “Current position”: “This is still a proposed earliest date, not a confirmed service date”; “The log makes no prediction about when those will be completed.”
counterevidence_and_boundaries.source_evidence: S1 calls April the “earliest possible passenger launch,” subject to conditions. S2 says the log “makes no prediction about when those items will be completed.”

reader_usefulness.reason: Provides actionable booking prerequisites and a clear recommendation, but repetition and excessive length reduce suitability as the requested desk note.
reader_usefulness.excerpt: “Recommended handling”: “Bookings should be accepted only after vessel delivery, successful trials, final passenger-service permission, a confirmed timetable and an actual booking release are all verified.”
reader_usefulness.source_evidence: S1 supplies delivery, trials and permission conditions; S2 records the missing permission, confirmed timetable and booking release.

condition_clues: After judgment: B's closing statement, “Independent review was not performed,” is a possible process-related clue; its checklist and table formatting could also suggest a structured workflow. Neither establishes a condition, and neither was rewarded as evidence of quality. A has no clear condition-identifying clue.
